title: Partial weight apply: dim mismatch — oncall log and post-incident notes
content:
INCIDENT SUMMARY:

Short summary:
During a scheduled canary rollout of model v2025-02-a, a subset of weight shards were applied with inconsistent tensor dimensions relative to the model graph on the canary nodes. This produced shape-mismatch errors in the first few attention layers when decoding longer prompts. Canary traffic experienced elevated failure traces and higher retry rates, triggering an on-call page. Automatic fallback routing successfully diverted production traffic to the previous model in < 3 min. No customer-facing downtime was observed for Hosted API customers, but internal SLIs for canary success degraded significantly.

Impact:
- Canary cluster: 18% of decode requests returned shape/validation errors during the window.
- Latency increased ~120ms p50 on affected canaries (due to retries/failovers).
- No production traffic routed to affected canaries due to routing fallback; no customer outages reported.

TIMELINE (UTC):
- 2025-02-12 02:08 — Automated rollout job started (rolling canary, 6 pods across 3 AZs).
- 2025-02-12 02:14 — Canary health check failures begin; Error rate alarm (canary-decode-errors) fires.
- 02:16 — On-call SRE (Sofia) pages. Initial dashboard shows decode error stacktraces containing tensor shape mismatch errors in "attn.q_proj" and "attn.kv_proj" layers.
- 02:22 — Quick triage: confirm only canary nodes affected; previous model commit still serving in primary pool.
- 02:30 — Rollout paused via orchestration API. Partial rollback initiated to previous model artifact on canaries.
- 02:32 — Routing policy triggered fallback; canary traffic routed away automatically.
- 02:40 — Rollback completed, canary cluster stabilized, error rates returned to baseline by 02:45.
- 02:50 — Post-incident coordination call started (eng-sre, runtime, release-engineering).

DETECTION DETAILS:
- Alerts: canary-decode-errors (threshold: >5% 2m), canary-healthcheck-fail (>3 nodes).
- Logs: stacktraces show ValueError: expected shape (256, 512) got (256, 496) during tensor reshape at model load/first-forward.
- Canary rollout logs revealed manifest mismatch warnings from the weight streamer: shard manifest version reported "v2" on controller but some shards labeled "v1" on storage nodes.

INITIAL HYPOTHESES CONSIDERED:
- Tokenizer/vocab mismatch (ruled out quickly: tokenizer version same as previous release and tests passed).
- Model graph mismatch vs weights (possible if release built with a different config).
- Weight shard corruption or partial apply due to streaming interruption.
- Incompatible quantization/precision (shapes still wrong — points to shard/manifest mismatch).

ROOT CAUSE (post-investigation):
A recent change in the weight publishing pipeline introduced optional per-shard compression and a manifest version flag. The rollout controller had a bug where it accepted the controller-level manifest version but did not verify per-shard manifest headers on each storage node prior to performing an in-place swap. During the weight push, two shards were uploaded with an older manifest schema (missing padding metadata) that resulted in truncated tensors on those shard files. When the runtime applied weights incrementally (streaming apply to limit memory pressure), the partial application left some layers with tensors of unexpected trailing dimension (e.g., 496 instead of 512) while other shards were correct. The runtime attempted to use the partially applied weights leading to shape-check failures at first forward passes.

WHY THIS PASSED CANARY CHECKS EARLIER:
- Unit-level checks verified checksums at the file-level but checksum logic ignored manifest-schema fields that changed how padding/stride are computed.
- The streaming apply process was optimized to avoid a full atomic swap of all shards (to reduce downtime). This optimization did not include a full shape validation across all tensors before switching traffic to the new weights.

IMMEDIATE MITIGATION TAKEN DURING INCIDENT:
- Paused rollout and initiated rollback to previous artifact (automated).
- Forced orchestration to perform full rehydrate (download + local validate) on all canary nodes before resuming any rollout.
- Isolated storage nodes that served the v1-manifest shards and flagged them for re-upload.

LONGER-TERM FIXES (planned / in-progress):
1) Weight publishing pipeline: enforce per-shard manifest schema validation at upload time and fail the publish if any shard uses an unsupported schema. (Owner: Maya S, ETA: 2025-02-22)
2) Runtime weight-apply path: add atomicity — create validated temporary workload-local checkpoint, perform a full shape/consistency check across all tensors, then do an atomic swap. If validation fails, abort and leave existing weights in place. (Owner: Ethan P, ETA: 2025-03-03)
3) Add a hard alert "weight-apply-shape-mismatch" triggered when any model process logs a shape validation failure during model load/first-forward. (Owner: SRE monitoring, ETA: 2025-02-20)
4) Update release orchestration to verify per-shard manifest versions and to run a dry-run shape validation across a canary replica before any traffic is routed. (Owner: Release Eng, ETA: 2025-02-25)

RUNBOOK/OPERATIONAL CHANGES (draft updates):
- Pre-rollout checklist additions:
  * Verify per-shard manifest versions match controller manifest (storage manifest headers).
  * Ensure new weight format compatibility test passes (shape/dtype/quantization).
  * If streaming apply is enabled, run full shape validation dry-run on at least 1 canary replica with a traffic shadow for 5 minutes.
- On-call playbook (new steps):
  * If decode shape errors observed: immediately pause rollout, disable streaming-apply, and switch to atomic rehydrate path.
  * If manifest mismatch found: mark storage nodes as suspect, escalate to release-engineering and storage team for reupload/rekey.

MONITORING & METRICS ADDED:
- weight_publish_manifest_mismatch_count (counter, per-artifact)
- weight_apply_validation_failures (counter, per-node, histogram of failed layers)
- canary_full_shape_validation_pass (gauge 0/1 per replica)

ACTION ITEMS (owners and due dates):
- Maya Singh: implement per-shard manifest schema enforcement in publisher pipeline. Due 2025-02-22.
- Ethan Park: implement atomic apply + full-shape-validation in runtime. Add unit tests for corner cases. Due 2025-03-03.
- SRE Monitoring (Liam O'Connor): create alerting rule and Grafana panels for weight_apply_validation_failures; add to runbook. Due 2025-02-20.
- Release Engineering: add manifest and shape dry-run step to rollout pipeline; block rollouts on dry-run failures. Due 2025-02-25.
- Documentation: update onboarding/release checklist + publish short postmortem note to Confluence (owner: Sofia Ramirez, Due 2025-02-18).

LESSONS LEARNED / NOTES:
- Optimizations that reduce rollout atomicity (streaming/partial apply) increase the surface area for subtle incompatibilities. Safety checks must be explicit and comprehensive.
- Filesystem-level checksums are insufficient when schema/metadata semantics change — tests must validate interpreted tensor shapes, not just bytes.
- Canary routing fallback worked as designed and prevented customer impact; keep investing in fast routing/health checks.

ATTACHMENTS / ARTIFACTS:
- Linked JIRA: JIRA-INF-4273 (investigation + follow-ups)
- Runtime fix PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/912
- Storage/manifest spec draft: Confluence: SR-Model-Rollouts (see section "manifest-schema-v2")

POSTMORTEM SEVERITY: P2 (impact limited to canary; potential for P1 if not caught before broader rollout).

LAST NOTES FROM ONCALL:
- Quick wins prioritized for next 10 days: alerting + publisher manifest enforcement.
- Major engineering work (atomic apply) tracked as runtime project — needs QA and integration tests with rollout pipeline.

If you are reading this as an owner of an action item, please update the ticket in JIRA-INF-4273 with progress and link PRs. Add questions/clarifications inline below.

---
Notes-to-self (raw oncall snippets):
- saw stacks: "reshape failed: expected 512 got 496" -> investigate shard offsets.
- storage node s3-proxy-7 had older agent version — reupload confirmed fixed.
- make dry-run cheap but representative (use small batch with longer prompt).
